originalGroup.material:
The bell at home

Owen gets a new bell for his bicycle. It is silver and makes a clear ringing sound. He wants to try it in the garden, but his little sister is asleep in her room beside the garden.

Dad asks him to wait. Owen puts the bell on the kitchen table and draws a picture of his bike instead. He colours the frame red and the wheels black.

When his sister wakes up, she comes to look at the picture. Then they go outside with Dad. Owen rings the bell once. His sister laughs and rings her toy bell too. The two bells make very different sounds.

originalGroup.material:
The red folder

Amira takes a red folder to her music lesson. It holds three pages of songs. On the bus, she puts it beside her on the seat. When she gets off, she remembers it just in time and picks it up.

At the music room, her teacher gives her a new page. "Put this behind the other songs," she says. Amira opens the folder, adds the page and closes it carefully.

At home, Mum asks which song she will practise first. Amira takes out the new one. It has a small picture of a boat at the top. She starts slowly, then sings it again with Mum.

originalGroup.material:
The little clay bird

Theo makes a small bird from clay at school. Its body is round and its tail is short. He adds two little wings, then asks the teacher where it should dry.

The teacher shows him a shelf by the wall. Theo puts his name on a piece of paper beside the bird. He does not write on its wet body.

The next day, the teacher says the bird needs more time. Theo looks at it but leaves it on the shelf. On Friday, he can take it home. He puts it in a small box with soft paper around it. Grandma opens the box and smiles at the bird's funny feet.

originalGroup.material:
Two maps for the picnic

Ella draws a map from her house to the picnic field. She puts the shop on the left and the bridge near the top. Her brother Max draws a second map. His shop is on the right because he is looking from the other end of the road.

They show both maps to Dad. He asks them to add a starting point and arrows. Now it is easier to see which way each map goes.

At the field, they put the maps under a stone so the wind cannot take them. After lunch, Max follows Ella's arrows home. She follows his. Both children arrive at their front door together.

originalGroup.material:
A hat for the snowman

In this winter story, two children make a snowman in their garden. Jo brings a small carrot for its nose. Her brother Nick brings two dark stones for its eyes.

The snowman has no hat. Nick wants to use Dad's warm wool hat, but Dad needs it for his walk. Jo finds an old flowerpot in the shed. They brush it clean and turn it upside down on the snowman's head.

Dad laughs when he comes outside. "That is a very tall hat," he says. Before leaving, he takes a photo. The children stand beside their snowman, each wearing their own wool hat in the cold air.

Dad laughs when he comes outside. "That is a very tall hat," he says. Before leaving, he takes a photo. The children stand beside their snowman, each wearing their own wool hat in the cold air.
questions.explanation: He keeps his warm hat; the snowman uses a pot.
